title: Lifting the Veil of Non-Stationarity in Financial Market

problem.claim: Financial price movement prediction is difficult because market data distributions shift over time.

gap.claim: Methods that assume stationarity have limited applicability to non-stationary markets.

contributions.claim: The Market-State Jump Diffusion Framework models market non-stationarity through explicit and implicit market-state jump diffusion processes.
The explicit process models diffusion, drift, and jump dynamics governed by latent market states using SDEs and neural networks.
A general modality synthesizer uses unified adversarial masking to complete missing modalities and fine-tune prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world stock and cryptocurrency datasets reportedly show that the method outperforms existing approaches in price movement prediction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Financial prediction is challenged by shifting market distributions.
MSJD addresses non-stationarity with explicit and implicit jump diffusion processes.
A modality synthesizer handles missing modalities and prediction fine-tuning.
The authors report superior performance on stock and cryptocurrency datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines explicit stochastic modeling with implicit multimodal representation learning for changing market conditions.

interpretation.claim: Combining interpretable process structure with flexible learned representations may help address distribution shift.

application.claim: Use explicit state-dependent dynamics alongside learned multimodal encoders when prediction environments are non-stationary.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination benefits settings outside financial price prediction.

unknowns: Dataset names, sizes, time periods, splits, and preprocessing are unspecified.
Baselines, metrics, quantitative gains, ablations, and statistical significance are unspecified.
